title: Content coverage: the user-facing half, thinner than the transport half
description:
Mark, 2026-11-22. Where mandated interop VISIBLY fails for users: not
refused messages, but messages that arrive as "unsupported content".

| Gap | Where it stands |
|---|---|
| Read receipts / message status | mimid-1wgh.11.11, deferred, "adopt later" |
| AV metadata | mimid-1wgh.14.1, deferred |
| Voice and video calls | largely outside mimi-content; a core feature of every app on the list |
| Typing, polls, location, stickers | not in content-10 |
| Attachments at volume | proxyDownload exists; Haven lists assets_ohttp unsupported |

Two of these are already beads deferred by decision (mimid-1wgh.44.31
and .44.46 respectively), which was the right call for a reference
implementation talking to one friendly peer. Under a mandate the
calculation changes, because a user who sees "unsupported content" does
not care which draft was unfinished.

Calls are the sharpest case: they are a core feature of every messenger
on the gatekeeper list and largely NOT in mimi-content, so this is a
specification gap rather than a mimid backlog item. Worth knowing before
anyone promises a date.

NOTE this is the group most affected by the decision on mimid-7yn7.1. A
conformance implementation needs to DECODE and JUDGE content, which
mimid largely does; it does not need to render a sticker. If Mark picks
the conformance path, most of this table stops being blocking.
notes: 2026-11-23: the calls row has a concrete shape now. mimi-content does have a 'session' disposition and §4.5 ExternalPart, and mimid already maps that to a JMAP VTC MessageAction both ways (project.rs:202-210, backend.rs:872-893). What is missing upstream is the semantics around it -- what a receiver does with a session part it cannot join, whether it is content or a live endpoint, lifetime, which schemes are meaningful, and any ringing or declining states. Never raised with the WG; see mimid-1wgh.37.106. Our own binding draft does not specify the mapping either: mimid-bcji.
